title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (AI Act)
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data (GDPR)

name: Provider
description: Develops an AI system or has one developed and places it on the market under its own name or trademark.

name: Deployer
description: Uses an AI system under its own authority, other than in a personal non-professional capacity.

children.text: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

heading: Minimum log content for biometric identification systems

children.text: For high-risk systems referred to in Annex III point 1(a), logging shall record at minimum: the period of each use (start and end date and time), the reference database against which input data was checked, the input data for which the search led to a match, and the identification of the natural persons involved in verifying the results.

Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control. The logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data.
Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.

claims.assertion: The system must be technically capable of recording events automatically across its lifetime.
The provider must keep those logs for at least six months, unless other Union or national law says otherwise.
claims.conditionalOn: Provider role; logs under the provider's control; applies from 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III systems.

claims.assertion: Where the logs contain personal data, they must not be kept longer than necessary for the purpose.
claims.conditionalOn: Any log containing personal data. Art. 12(3) makes this unavoidable for biometric systems.

claims.assertion: The deployer must keep the logs it controls for at least six months — the same floor the provider carries under Art. 19, but a separate duty on a separate party.
claims.conditionalOn: Deployer role; logs under the deployer’s control. Applies from 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III systems.

evidenceHint: A retention schedule naming the six-month floor, the purpose justifying the chosen period, and the deletion mechanism that enforces the ceiling. Auditors ask for the schedule and a sample deletion record, not a policy statement.

summary: AI Act sets a six-month floor for log retention; GDPR sets a necessity ceiling on the same logs
Art. 19 applies from 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III systems but 2 Aug 2028 for Annex I systems

name: Biometric access control for a logistics hub
description: Face matching against an employee reference database at site entrances. Built in Kazakhstan, deployed at a client site in Poland.

name: Tool-calling support agent
description: LLM agent that reads tickets and executes refunds through an internal API. The case none of these texts were drafted for.

heading: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems

children.text: An AI system is high-risk where it is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, and that product must undergo third-party conformity assessment under that legislation.

Annex I numbers its items 1 to 21. Item 1 (Directive 2006/42/EC on machinery) is struck by amendment and item 21 (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery, repealing Directive 2006/42/EC) is added, so twenty items are live.

obligation: Determine whether the product falls under Annex I harmonisation legislation

claims.assertion: A system is high-risk where it is a safety component of, or is itself, a product covered by Annex I legislation that needs third-party conformity assessment.
claims.conditionalOn: Turns on whether your product type appears in Annex I at all.

claims.assertion: Annex I lists twenty live items under a numbering that runs to 21, because item 1 was deleted and item 21 added by amendment.
claims.conditionalOn: Machinery is the affected case: Directive 2006/42/EC was replaced by Regulation (EU) 2023/1230.

evidenceHint: Name the Annex I item your product falls under, by instrument, not by item number. Numbers move when the annex is amended; the instrument does not.

summary: Annex I numbering runs to 21 but only 20 items are live after the machinery amendment
rationale: Sanity Context raised this while indexing: an entry stated Annex I lists 21 instruments, and the source shows 20. Verified against artificialintelligenceact.eu on 2026-09-19 — the numbering does run 1 to 21, item 1 (Directive 2006/42/EC) is struck and item 21 (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230) is added, leaving 20 live items. Cite instruments, not item numbers. Note that Context also proposed a Section A / Section B split of 12 and 8; that part is NOT verified here, because the official EUR-Lex text could not be retrieved, and it is deliberately left out of this record. The detection was right and its arithmetic was not independently confirmed — which is why this decision carries a name.

heading: Deployer duty to keep automatically generated logs

children.text: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data.
